2000_election.title: 2000 US Presidential Election
2000_election.description: The closest presidential election in modern US history. Bush v. Gore decided by 537 votes in Florida after a Supreme Court decision halting the recount. Shaped foreign policy, climate policy, judicial appointments, and the trajectory of American polarization for decades.

bush_wins.description: George W. Bush wins after Supreme Court halts Florida recount

gore_wins.description: Al Gore wins after full Florida recount
gore_wins.explanation: Butterfly ballot confusion resolved, Gore carries Florida by ~2,000 votes

contested_months.description: Constitutional crisis — no clear president until February 2001
contested_months.explanation: Supreme Court ruling ignored, dueling electors, House decides

2001_911.title: September 11 Attacks
2001_911.description: Coordinated al-Qaeda hijackings of four commercial aircraft. Two struck the World Trade Center, one hit the Pentagon, one crashed in Pennsylvania. 2,977 killed. The defining event shaping US foreign policy, civil liberties, and global security architecture for the entire century.

historical_full.description: All four hijackings succeed; WTC, Pentagon struck; UA93 crashes in PA

partial_success.description: 1-2 flights hit targets; others intercepted or failed
partial_success.explanation: Earlier FAA response or passenger awareness prevents full attack

single_attack.description: Only WTC North Tower struck; other plots foiled in execution
single_attack.explanation: Rapid military response after first impact; heightened cabin awareness

plot_disrupted.explanation: FBI/CIA intelligence sharing catches plotters; Phoenix/Minneapolis memos acted on

worse_outcome.description: All four flights hit targets including US Capitol
worse_outcome.explanation: UA93 passenger revolt fails; Capitol struck during session

2001_china_wto.title: China Joins WTO
2001_china_wto.description: China's accession to the World Trade Organization, enabling massive export-led growth. Controversial due to minimal enforcement of IP and currency manipulation conditions.

historical_full_accession.description: Full WTO accession with minimal enforcement of conditions

conditional_accession.description: WTO accession with strict IP and currency conditions enforced

no_accession.description: China rejected from WTO; pursues bilateral trade

2001_dotcom_aftermath.title: Dot-Com Crash Aftermath
2001_dotcom_aftermath.description: Federal Reserve response to dot-com bust and post-9/11 recession. Greenspan cut rates aggressively to 1%, which many argue seeded the housing bubble that led to the 2008 financial crisis.

historical_slow_rates_cut.description: Greenspan cuts rates to 1%; loose monetary policy seeds housing bubble

faster_recovery.description: Tech sector rebounds quickly; moderate rate cuts
faster_recovery.explanation: Dot-com losses absorbed faster than expected

2002_security_overreach.title: Post-9/11 Security Architecture
2002_security_overreach.description: Even without a full Iraq invasion, 9/11 (or its partial equivalent) triggers a massive security state expansion. Patriot Act, DHS creation, TSA, warrantless wiretapping. The question is how far it goes.

historical_expansion.description: Full Patriot Act, DHS creation, TSA, warrantless surveillance programs

moderate_expansion.description: Security measures enacted with sunset clauses and judicial oversight

aggressive_overreach.description: Extreme security measures; internment discussions; massive civil liberties erosion

restrained_response.description: Targeted counterterrorism with civil liberties prioritized

historical_boom_then_bust.description: BRICS economies boom 2003-2011, then stagnate except China

china_only.description: Only China grows significantly; others stagnate

2003_columbia.title: Columbia Shuttle Disaster
2003_columbia.description: Space Shuttle Columbia disintegrates on re-entry. Seven crew killed. Accelerates the end of the shuttle program and reshapes NASA's future direction — toward Constellation, then cancellation, then commercial crew.

historical_disaster.description: Shuttle destroyed on re-entry; program eventually ends

averted.description: Foam strike detected in orbit; crew rescued via ISS rendezvous

worse_earlier.description: Earlier shuttle disaster in 2001 accelerates end-of-program timeline

program_cancelled_immediately.description: Congress kills shuttle program within a year of disaster

2003_genome_aftermath.title: Post-Genome Era
2003_genome_aftermath.description: Human Genome Project completed. The $1000 genome is a decade away. Personal genomics, pharmacogenomics, and genetic privacy debates begin.

historical_slow_translation.description: Genomics advances but clinical translation is slow; $1000 genome by 2014

rapid_personalized_medicine.description: Personalized medicine arrives by 2015; pharmacogenomics becomes standard of care

genetic_privacy_crisis.description: Genetic discrimination becomes major issue; insurance and employers use genetic data

open_science_model.description: Open access to genetic data accelerates research worldwide

overhyped_stalls.description: Funding dries up when miracle cures don't materialize; genomics enters winter

2003_iraq.title: Iraq War Decision
2003_iraq.description: Decision to invade Iraq based on WMD claims and terrorism links. No WMDs found. Prolonged occupation, ~200,000+ Iraqi civilian deaths, ISIS emergence, massive erosion of US credibility. Arguably the single highest-leverage policy decision of the century.

full_invasion.description: US-led coalition invades Iraq; Saddam toppled

limited_strikes.description: US conducts air strikes against suspected WMD sites only

diplomatic_resolution.description: UN inspections continue; no military action taken
diplomatic_resolution.explanation: Inspectors given more time; WMD claims debunked before invasion

delayed_invasion.description: Invasion delayed to 2004-2005 with broader coalition

2003_opioid_crisis.title: Opioid Crisis
2003_opioid_crisis.description: OxyContin-driven opioid epidemic begins. Purdue Pharma's aggressive marketing of prescription opioids leads to addiction epidemic, eventually killing 700,000+ Americans.

historical_epidemic.description: Opioid epidemic kills 700K+ by 2030; fentanyl wave devastates

fentanyl_prevented.description: Fentanyl wave prevented through border enforcement and treatment

treatment_focused.description: Addiction treated as health issue early; harm reduction

historical_expansion.description: US drone strike program expands globally

limited_use.description: Drone warfare limited to active war zones

2004_hurricane_season.title: Record Hurricane Season
2004_hurricane_season.description: Four major hurricanes hit Florida in six weeks. Exposes FEMA weaknesses and sets the stage for the Katrina catastrophe a year later.

historical_four_storms.description: Four major hurricanes hit Florida; FEMA weaknesses exposed

mild_season.description: Fewer storms; FEMA not tested and remains complacent

catastrophic_fifth.description: Category 5 hurricane hits Miami directly; massive destruction

2004_social_media.title: Social Media Emergence
2004_social_media.description: Launch of Facebook, followed by Twitter, YouTube, and others. Ad-driven, engagement-maximizing social media platforms reshape politics, culture, mental health, and information ecosystems.

subscription_model.description: Subscription-based social media; less engagement optimization
subscription_model.explanation: Early platforms charge $5/month; slower growth but healthier discourse

decentralized.explanation: Open protocols prevail over walled gardens

regulated_early.description: EU-style regulation applied early; algorithmic transparency required

2004_tsunami.title: Indian Ocean Tsunami
2004_tsunami.description: 9.1 earthquake triggers tsunami killing 230,000 across 14 countries. Creates the Indian Ocean early warning system. Reshapes international disaster response and aid architecture.

historical_catastrophe.description: 230K dead across 14 countries; no warning system existed

warning_system_existed.description: Hypothetical early detection system in place; deaths reduced to ~30K

worse_timing.description: Hits during peak tourist season; 400K+ dead

triggers_reform.description: Historical devastation leads to major international disaster preparedness reforms

2005_katrina.title: Hurricane Katrina Response
2005_katrina.description: Hurricane Katrina devastates Gulf Coast. FEMA response widely condemned as catastrophic failure. Exposes racial and economic inequalities, erodes trust in federal government.

catastrophic_failure.description: FEMA fails catastrophically; 1,800+ die; New Orleans flooded for weeks

exemplary_response.explanation: Mandatory evacuation enforced; FEMA fully resourced

worse_failure.description: Even slower response; 3,000+ die; martial law declared

historical_slow_build.description: Slow build of racial consciousness; sets stage for BLM

immediate_reform.description: Katrina triggers immediate racial justice reforms

earlier_blm.description: Mass racial justice movement emerges in 2006-2008

2006_cloud.title: Cloud Computing / AWS
2006_cloud.description: Amazon Web Services launches, creating the cloud computing paradigm. Enables startups, AI research, and pandemic-era remote work.

historical_hyperscaler.description: AWS, Azure, GCP dominate; hyperscaler model wins

open_source_cloud.description: Open source cloud platforms win over proprietary

historical_nuclear_state.description: North Korea becomes de facto nuclear state

frozen_program.description: Nuclear program frozen at early stage

preemptive_strike.description: US or allied preemptive strike on nuclear facilities

nuclear_sale.description: North Korea sells nuclear materials to non-state actors

2007_iphone.title: Smartphone Revolution
2007_iphone.description: Apple launches iPhone, catalyzing the smartphone era. Mobile internet transforms communication, commerce, social media, and daily life globally.

historical_apple_led.description: iPhone launches smartphone revolution; iOS/Android duopoly

open_platform_wins.description: Open mobile platforms dominate over walled gardens
open_platform_wins.explanation: Linux-based open phones gain traction before iPhone

fragmented_market.description: No dominant platform; feature phones persist longer

2008_beijing_olympics.title: Beijing Olympics
2008_beijing_olympics.description: China's global coming-out party. $44B investment. Showcases Chinese organizational capability and ambition. Shapes how China sees itself and how the world sees China for the next decade.

historical_success.description: Spectacular games; China arrives on world stage

boycott.description: Major Western boycott over human rights record

2008_financial_crisis.title: 2008 Financial Crisis
2008_financial_crisis.description: Collapse of Lehman Brothers triggers global financial crisis. Housing bubble burst, credit freeze, massive bailouts. The deepest recession since the Great Depression, reshaping economic policy and fueling populist movements worldwide.

historical_severe.description: Lehman collapse; global credit freeze; deep recession

contained_early.description: Bear Stearns triggers earlier intervention; Lehman saved
contained_early.explanation: Fed acts more aggressively in March 2008

great_depression_2.description: No TARP; cascading bank failures; global depression

mild_recession.description: Better regulation prevented worst; mild downturn
mild_recession.explanation: Derivatives regulated post-Enron; housing bubble smaller

2008_fracking.title: US Shale / Fracking Revolution
2008_fracking.description: Hydraulic fracturing transforms US from energy importer to the world's largest oil and gas producer. Geopolitical implications are enormous — reduces Middle East leverage, delays renewable transition, but also enables coal-to-gas switching that reduces emissions.

historical_boom.description: US becomes energy independent by 2019; largest oil and gas producer

regulated_heavily.description: Environmental concerns limit fracking; US remains net energy importer

technology_fails.description: Shale wells deplete faster than expected; fracking boom fizzles by 2015

earlier_boom.description: Fracking scales 3 years earlier; US energy independent by 2016

environmental_catastrophe.description: Major groundwater contamination event triggers nationwide fracking ban

2008_obama_election.title: 2008 US Presidential Election
2008_obama_election.description: In the base spec, this is implicit (the 2016 node references the prior cycle). Making it explicit allows the Obama/McCain choice to affect the 2009-2015 period independently of the financial crisis.

obama_wins.description: Barack Obama wins presidency; first Black president

mccain_wins.description: John McCain wins; Republican continuity through financial crisis

third_party_factor.description: Ron Paul independent run splits Republican vote

2009_twitter_politics.title: Twitter Becomes Political Infrastructure
2009_twitter_politics.description: Twitter's role in the Iranian Green Movement (2009) establishes social media as political infrastructure. By 2016, it's the primary channel for political communication, radicalization, and manipulation.

historical_political_capture.description: Twitter becomes the political town square for real-time discourse and outrage

remains_niche.description: Twitter stays a niche tech and media platform, never captures political discourse
remains_niche.explanation: Without political adoption, Twitter remains smaller and less influential

moderated_early.description: Aggressive content moderation from 2012 prevents weaponization of the platform
moderated_early.explanation: Twitter invests heavily in moderation; political manipulation is curtailed early

decentralized_alternative.description: Open protocol wins; no single company controls political discourse
decentralized_alternative.explanation: Federated microblogging (like Mastodon) gains traction early

government_regulated.description: FCC-style regulation of political speech on platforms enacted early
government_regulated.explanation: Platforms treated as public utilities with fairness doctrine requirements

2010_arab_spring.title: Arab Spring
2010_arab_spring.description: Wave of pro-democracy protests across the Middle East and North Africa. Tunisia succeeds; Egypt's revolution leads to military coup; Libya and Syria descend into civil war. ~500K+ dead in resulting conflicts.

historical_mixed.description: Tunisia succeeds; Egypt coup; Libya/Syria civil war

broader_success.explanation: Egypt military stays neutral; international support stronger

2010_deepwater_horizon.title: Deepwater Horizon Oil Spill
2010_deepwater_horizon.description: Largest marine oil spill in history. 11 workers killed, 4.9M barrels spilled into Gulf of Mexico. Reshapes drilling regulation and accelerates anti-fossil-fuel sentiment.

historical_spill.description: 4.9M barrels spilled; 87 days to cap the well

prevented_by_regulation.description: Stricter MMS oversight catches blowout preventer failure before disaster

worse_uncontained.description: Takes 6+ months to cap; ecological catastrophe in Gulf

accelerates_transition.description: Spill triggers aggressive pivot to renewable energy investment

historical_austerity.description: Troika-imposed austerity; slow recovery; Greek suffering

fiscal_union.explanation: Germany agrees to mutual debt; faster recovery

grexit.description: Greece exits the euro; contagion spreads

2010_haiti.title: Haiti Earthquake
2010_haiti.description: 7.0 earthquake kills 220,000-316,000 in the poorest country in the Western Hemisphere. International response is massive but widely criticized as ineffective. Shapes development aid debate.

historical_catastrophe.description: Massive earthquake devastates Haiti; international response widely criticized

better_response.description: More effective international aid coordination saves lives

build_back_better.description: Haiti actually rebuilt with resilient infrastructure

aid_scandal.description: Red Cross and NGO failures dominate the narrative

2010_local_news_death.title: Collapse of Local Journalism
2010_local_news_death.description: Craigslist kills classified ad revenue. Google/Facebook capture digital ad spending. Local newspapers close at the rate of 2 per week. "News deserts" cover 1/3 of US counties by 2020. Arguably the single largest structural driver of polarization — without local accountability journalism, national outrage media fills the void.

historical_collapse.description: 2,500+ newspapers close 2005-2030; news deserts cover a third of US counties

public_funding_saves.description: BBC-model public funding for local news sustains accountability journalism
public_funding_saves.explanation: Congress creates a Corporation for Local News; local papers receive federal support

platform_revenue_sharing.description: Google and Facebook forced to share advertising revenue with news publishers
platform_revenue_sharing.explanation: Australia-style legislation passes in the US and EU, funding local newsrooms

nonprofit_model_wins.description: ProPublica-style nonprofit journalism scales to fill the local news gap
nonprofit_model_wins.explanation: Philanthropic funding and community support create sustainable local outlets

slow_decline.description: Local news declines gradually; some newspapers survive through digital transition
slow_decline.explanation: Paywalls and digital subscriptions slow the bleeding enough to maintain coverage

2010_spacex_falcon9.title: SpaceX and Reusable Rocketry
2010_spacex_falcon9.description: Falcon 9 first flight. First successful landing 2015. Reduces launch costs by 10x. Without reusable rockets, nothing else in the space timeline happens.

historical_success.description: SpaceX succeeds with Falcon 9; reusable rocketry slashes launch costs by 10x
historical_success.explanation: Falcon 9 flies 2010, first landing 2015; opens commercial space era

delayed_5_years.description: Technical challenges delay reusable rocketry to ~2015; space timeline shifts
delayed_5_years.explanation: Engine failures and landing difficulties push the reusability milestone back five years

spacex_fails.description: SpaceX fails; ULA and Arianespace continue at high cost
spacex_fails.explanation: Company cannot sustain funding after early failures; legacy providers retain monopoly

multiple_competitors.description: Blue Origin, Rocket Lab achieve parity with SpaceX; competitive market emerges
multiple_competitors.explanation: Multiple companies independently develop reusable rockets; faster innovation through competition

government_only.description: Private space doesn't take off; NASA and ESA dominate with high-cost launches
government_only.explanation: Regulatory barriers and risk aversion prevent commercial space from flourishing

historical_escalation.description: Stuxnet discovered; opens era of state-sponsored cyber weapons

cyber_arms_race.description: Open cyber arms race between major powers

deterrence_established.description: Cyber norms and deterrence framework established

iran_retaliates.description: Iran retaliates with major cyberattack on US infrastructure

historical_leaks.description: Manning leaks; diplomatic cables; Assange saga

no_manning_leak.description: Manning doesn't leak; WikiLeaks stays marginal

more_damaging.description: Even more damaging leaks of intelligence operations

whistleblower_protection.description: Leak leads to strong whistleblower protections

2011_bin_laden.title: Bin Laden Operation
2011_bin_laden.description: The hunt for Osama bin Laden culminates in a decision about how to act on intelligence locating him in Abbottabad, Pakistan. The outcome affects US credibility, counterterrorism trajectory, and Pakistan relations.

successful_raid.description: Navy SEAL raid in Abbottabad kills bin Laden; body buried at sea

raid_fails.description: Helicopter crash aborts mission; bin Laden escapes Abbottabad compound

diplomatic_capture.description: Pakistan cooperates in joint operation; bin Laden captured alive and tried

not_found.description: Intelligence never pinpoints compound; bin Laden remains at large

historical_recurring_crises.description: Repeated debt ceiling crises; brinkmanship becomes norm

actual_default.description: US actually defaults briefly; market chaos

grand_bargain.description: Bipartisan grand bargain on spending and taxes

historical_meltdown.description: Three reactor meltdowns; global nuclear retreat

contained_quickly.description: Backup systems work; minimal radiation release

historical_intervention_chaos.description: NATO intervenes; Gaddafi killed; Libya descends into chaos

no_intervention.description: No Western intervention; Gaddafi suppresses revolt

full_commitment.description: Full commitment to post-Gaddafi state building

arab_league_led.description: Arab League leads intervention with Western support

2011_occupy.title: Occupy Wall Street
2011_occupy.description: Protest movement against economic inequality. "We are the 99%." Failed to produce policy change but reshaped political vocabulary and set the stage for both Sanders and Trump populism.

historical_fizzle.description: Protests gain attention but produce no lasting institutional impact

lasting_movement.description: Occupy evolves into a permanent political force

policy_wins.description: Occupy achieves financial regulation or progressive tax reform

co_opted.description: Movement energy absorbed into existing political parties

backlash.description: Occupy triggers anti-protest legislation and public backlash

2011_solar_revolution.title: Solar Cost Revolution
2011_solar_revolution.description: Solyndra bankruptcy embarrasses US solar policy, but Chinese manufacturing drives solar costs down 90% over the decade — the fastest cost decline of any energy technology in history.

historical_cost_collapse.description: Solar drops below coal by 2020; fastest energy cost decline in history

slower_decline.description: Solar cost parity delayed to 2028; fossil fuels retain dominance longer

manufacturing_distributed.description: Non-Chinese solar manufacturing develops; slower but more resilient supply chain

accelerated_by_policy.description: Carbon pricing accelerates solar adoption beyond historical pace

trade_wars_slow.description: Tariffs on Chinese panels slow global solar deployment

2012_deep_learning.title: Deep Learning / AlexNet Breakthrough
2012_deep_learning.description: AlexNet wins ImageNet competition by massive margin, proving deep neural networks + GPUs can solve vision problems at scale. Triggers modern AI revolution.

historical_gpu_revolution.description: Deep learning + GPUs transform AI; massive investment follows

slower_progress.description: Deep learning works but adoption is gradual

alternative_paradigm.description: Different AI approach (probabilistic, symbolic-neural hybrid) wins

compute_bottleneck.description: GPU scaling hits hard limits; progress stalls

2012_instagram.title: Instagram / Visual Social Media
2012_instagram.description: Facebook acquires Instagram. Visual social media creates unprecedented body image pressure, particularly for teen girls. Internal Facebook research (later leaked) shows Instagram is "toxic" for teen mental health.

historical_toxicity.description: Instagram drives teen mental health crisis through comparison culture and body image pressure

stays_independent.description: Instagram not acquired by Facebook; develops with different incentives
stays_independent.explanation: Without Facebook's engagement optimization, Instagram evolves more slowly but healthily

age_restrictions_enforced.description: Under-16 ban on social media actually enforced through age verification
age_restrictions_enforced.explanation: COPPA-style legislation with real enforcement protects minors from social media harms

design_for_wellbeing.description: Platform redesigned to reduce social comparison and promote wellbeing
design_for_wellbeing.explanation: Hidden likes, reduced filters, and anti-comparison features become standard

backlash_kills_growth.description: Youth reject visual social media after early backlash against comparison culture
backlash_kills_growth.explanation: Cultural shift against performative social media limits Instagram's influence

2012_sandy_hook.title: Sandy Hook / Gun Control
2012_sandy_hook.description: Mass shooting at elementary school kills 26 including 20 children. Fails to produce federal gun legislation despite overwhelming public support. Crystallizes the gun control gridlock.

historical_no_legislation.description: Manchin-Toomey fails; no federal gun legislation passes

assault_weapons_ban.description: Manchin-Toomey passes; assault weapons restricted nationwide

no_shooting.description: Sandy Hook shooting does not occur

cultural_shift.description: March For Our Lives energy happens six years earlier

backlash_more_guns.description: Defensive gun purchases spike; NRA strengthens politically

historical_consolidation.description: Xi abolishes term limits; consolidates power

economic_liberalization.description: China prioritizes economic liberalization over control

2012_youtube_radicalization.title: YouTube Recommendation Radicalization
2012_youtube_radicalization.description: YouTube's recommendation algorithm begins systematically pushing users toward increasingly extreme content. The "rabbit hole" effect radicalizes millions over the next decade, from alt-right to QAnon to anti-vax.

historical_radicalization.description: Algorithm optimizes for engagement, systematically driving users toward extremism

algorithm_fixed.description: YouTube identifies and fixes the radicalization pipeline by 2015
algorithm_fixed.explanation: Internal research leads to algorithm changes prioritizing quality over engagement

worse_pipeline.description: Radicalization accelerates into real-world violence earlier and more severely

competitor_breaks_model.description: TikTok-style competitor emerges without the same radicalization dynamics
competitor_breaks_model.explanation: A short-form video competitor captures attention without rabbit-hole algorithms

regulated.description: FTC investigation forces algorithmic transparency and changes
regulated.explanation: Regulatory pressure leads to mandatory algorithm audits

historical_extended_zirp.description: Near-zero rates for 12+ years; massive QE

early_normalization.description: Rate hikes begin 2014; slower but more stable growth

negative_rates_us.description: US follows Europe into negative rates

fiscal_over_monetary.description: Fiscal stimulus replaces monetary; infrastructure spending

2013_boston_marathon.title: Boston Marathon Bombing
2013_boston_marathon.description: Pressure cooker bombs at marathon finish line. 3 killed, 264 injured. Demonstrates domestic radicalization threat and the "lone wolf" problem.

historical_attack.description: Pressure cooker bombs at finish line; 3 dead, 264 injured

plot_disrupted.description: FBI tips prevent the attack before it occurs

larger_attack.description: More sophisticated device causes significantly more casualties

no_attack.description: Tsarnaev brothers never radicalize; no attack planned

historical_speculative.description: $2T+ speculative asset class; minimal real-world currency use

becomes_real_currency.description: Crypto becomes actual medium of exchange

regulated_early.description: Heavy regulation from 2015; crypto as regulated asset

stablecoin_dominance.description: Stablecoins and CBDCs dominate; Bitcoin marginalized

2013_nuclear_policy_shift.title: Post-Fukushima Nuclear Policy Shift
2013_nuclear_policy_shift.description: In the aftermath of Fukushima, nations make pivotal decisions about nuclear energy. Germany commits to full phase-out by 2022. Japan shuts all 54 reactors. France debates reducing nuclear share. These decisions lock in fossil fuel dependence or accelerate renewables, with consequences lasting decades.

historical_retreat.description: Germany phases out nuclear; Japan offline for years; global nuclear capacity stalls

nuclear_renaissance.description: Nations double down on nuclear with improved safety; new builds accelerate

selective_phaseout.description: Only oldest reactors retired; new safety standards enable continued operation

accelerated_shutdown.description: Global anti-nuclear movement forces rapid closures; coal fills the gap

smr_pivot.description: Fukushima triggers pivot to small modular reactors; safer design paradigm

2013_pope_francis.title: Pope Francis Election
2013_pope_francis.description: Cardinal Jorge Bergoglio elected as Pope Francis, the first Latin American pope. His papacy emphasizes social justice, climate action (Laudato Si encyclical, 2015), and interfaith dialogue, shifting global Catholic influence toward the Global South and environmental stewardship.

historical_election.description: Francis elected; Laudato Si shifts Catholic discourse on climate and inequality

conservative_pope.description: A doctrinally conservative pope is elected; no climate encyclical
conservative_pope.explanation: Conclave selects a traditionalist European cardinal

radical_reform_pope.description: Francis pushes even further reforms including structural Church changes
radical_reform_pope.explanation: Papacy embraces sweeping modernization of Church governance

no_significant_impact.description: New pope has limited global political influence
no_significant_impact.explanation: Papacy focuses inward on Church administration

climate_leadership.description: Francis becomes the dominant global voice on climate, accelerating action
climate_leadership.explanation: Laudato Si triggers a broader moral mobilization beyond Catholic communities

2013_snowden.title: Snowden Revelations
2013_snowden.description: Edward Snowden leaks massive trove of NSA surveillance documents. Reveals scope of mass surveillance programs. Sparks global debate on privacy, security, and government overreach.

historical_leak.description: Snowden reveals NSA mass surveillance programs

2013_streaming.title: Streaming and Media Fragmentation
2013_streaming.description: Netflix original content (House of Cards, 2013) marks the end of shared media experiences. The monoculture fractures into niches. People stop watching the same news, same shows, same reality.

historical_fragmentation.description: Streaming services fragment the shared media landscape into algorithmic niches

shared_experiences_persist.description: Broadcast TV remains dominant longer; shared cultural reference points maintained
shared_experiences_persist.explanation: Streaming grows slowly; network TV retains majority viewership through 2020

hyper_fragmentation.description: Algorithmic personalization creates individual media realities with no overlap

public_media_strengthened.description: PBS/BBC model scales; shared reference points and trusted journalism maintained
public_media_strengthened.explanation: Public media investment grows; serves as common ground across political divides

creator_economy.description: Individual creators replace media institutions entirely
creator_economy.explanation: YouTube and podcast creators become primary information and entertainment sources

historical_no_strike.description: Obama doesn't enforce red line; Russia brokers deal

limited_strike.description: Limited US strikes against chemical weapons facilities

full_intervention.description: Full US military intervention in Syria

diplomatic_only.description: Diplomatic solution; Assad remains but chemical weapons removed

historical_wave.description: BLM emerges 2014; explodes 2020 after George Floyd

sustained_reform.description: BLM achieves sustained policing and justice reforms

no_movement.description: No mass racial justice movement emerges

2014_crimea.title: Crimea Annexation
2014_crimea.description: Russia annexes Crimea from Ukraine after Euromaidan revolution. First major land grab in Europe since WWII. Reshapes European security and sets stage for 2022 full-scale invasion.

failed_operation.explanation: Ukraine had more time to prepare; Western intelligence warning

negotiated_autonomy.description: Crimea gets autonomy within Ukraine through negotiation

full_eastern_invasion.description: Russia takes Crimea plus Donbas in 2014

historical_decline.description: US life expectancy declines; unprecedented for developed nation

public_health_response.description: Public health system mobilizes; treatment expansion

2014_ebola.title: West Africa Ebola Outbreak
2014_ebola.description: Largest Ebola outbreak in history. 28,600 cases, 11,325 deaths. Exposed weaknesses in global pandemic preparedness — lessons that were largely forgotten by the time COVID arrived.

historical_outbreak.description: 28,600 cases, 11,325 deaths in West Africa; lessons largely forgotten

contained_early.description: WHO responds faster; deaths kept under 1,000

global_spread.description: Ebola reaches major cities outside Africa

preparedness_legacy.description: Outbreak triggers lasting global pandemic preparedness investment

2014_flint_water.title: Flint Water Crisis
2014_flint_water.description: Flint, Michigan switches its water source to the Flint River to cut costs, leading to lead contamination affecting nearly 100,000 residents. Exposes systemic infrastructure decay, environmental racism, and government indifference to predominantly Black communities. Becomes a symbol of institutional failure in America.

historical_crisis.description: Lead contamination discovered late; slow government response; lasting health impacts

early_detection.description: Water quality issues detected within weeks; source switched back immediately
early_detection.explanation: EPA or state regulators catch the problem before widespread exposure

national_infrastructure_reform.description: Crisis triggers massive federal infrastructure investment
national_infrastructure_reform.explanation: Flint becomes catalyst for bipartisan infrastructure legislation

crisis_ignored.description: Federal government does not intervene; crisis deepens for years
crisis_ignored.explanation: Political indifference prevents any meaningful response

widespread_contamination.description: Similar crises emerge in multiple US cities simultaneously
widespread_contamination.explanation: Aging infrastructure fails across several underfunded municipalities

2014_gain_of_function.title: Gain-of-Function Research Debate
2014_gain_of_function.description: US government imposes moratorium on gain-of-function research after lab safety incidents. Dual-use research of concern sparks fierce debate between virologists and biosecurity experts. Whether risky virus research is regulated or continues has enormous implications for future pandemic risk.

historical_partial_moratorium.description: US moratorium 2014-2017; research resumes with modest oversight improvements

strict_global_ban.description: International treaty bans gain-of-function research; enforced through inspections

unregulated_expansion.description: Research expands to dozens of labs worldwide with minimal oversight

transparent_oversight.description: Robust international oversight framework balances research benefits and risks

lab_leak_event.description: Accidental lab release causes regional outbreak; triggers global crackdown

2014_gamergate.title: Gamergate / Online Harassment Weaponization
2014_gamergate.description: Gamergate controversy establishes the playbook for coordinated online harassment campaigns as political tools. The tactics pioneered here — doxxing, brigading, manufactured outrage — become standard in 2016 election interference and beyond.

historical_weaponization.description: Online harassment tactics become standard political weapons beyond gaming

contained_to_gaming.description: Harassment stays within gaming communities and does not spread to politics
contained_to_gaming.explanation: Mainstream media ignores the controversy; tactics never gain wider adoption

platform_crackdown.description: Reddit and Twitter crack down aggressively; harassment tactics fail to spread
platform_crackdown.explanation: Platforms ban coordinated harassment campaigns early, preventing normalization

2021_suez_canal.title: Suez Canal Blockage (Ever Given)
2021_suez_canal.description: The container ship Ever Given runs aground in the Suez Canal, blocking one of the world's most critical trade arteries for six days. The incident visualizes global supply chain fragility for a mass audience and accelerates discussions about trade route diversification and resilience.

historical_brief_blockage.description: Six-day blockage; $9B daily trade disruption; brief supply chain shock

extended_blockage.description: Ship stuck for weeks; global supply chains severely disrupted
extended_blockage.explanation: Salvage operations fail repeatedly; canal requires months of dredging

no_incident.description: Ever Given transits canal without incident
no_incident.explanation: Slightly different wind conditions prevent grounding

supply_chain_reform_catalyst.description: Blockage triggers major global supply chain diversification investment
supply_chain_reform_catalyst.explanation: Nations and corporations invest heavily in alternative routes and nearshoring

cascading_trade_crisis.description: Blockage combines with other disruptions to trigger a global trade crisis
cascading_trade_crisis.explanation: Simultaneous port congestion, COVID backlogs, and geopolitical tensions compound

permanent_reshoring.description: Crisis triggers permanent supply chain restructuring

worse_collapse.description: Critical shortages in food, medicine, semiconductors

historical_mainstreaming.description: Far-right parties enter mainstream across Europe

contained.description: Right-wing populism contained by centrist coalitions

governing_majority.description: Far-right gains governing majority in major EU country

2022_fusion_ignition.title: Fusion Ignition Achievement
2022_fusion_ignition.description: National Ignition Facility achieves fusion ignition — more energy out than laser energy in. But commercial fusion is decades away. Or is it?

historical_milestone.description: Scientific success; commercial fusion remains 2050+ prospect

accelerated_timeline.description: Private fusion companies achieve breakeven by 2035; commercial reactors by 2042

dead_end.description: Ignition was a one-off; fusion cannot be economically scaled

manhattan_project_2.description: Government crash program accelerates fusion; first reactor by 2038

private_sector_wins.description: Startup-driven fusion race; Commonwealth or TAE first commercial reactor by 2040

historical_high_then_controlled.description: Inflation peaks 9%; aggressive rate hikes bring it down by 2024

stagflation.description: High inflation persists with stagnant growth

2022_jwst.title: James Webb Space Telescope
2022_jwst.description: NASA's James Webb Space Telescope begins delivering unprecedented deep-field images of the early universe after a flawless deployment at L2. The $10B telescope represents a generational leap in astronomical capability, inspiring scientific wonder and renewing public interest in space exploration.

historical_success.description: Flawless deployment; stunning images; major discoveries in exoplanet atmospheres

deployment_failure.description: Critical deployment mechanism fails; telescope is partially or fully inoperable
deployment_failure.explanation: One of 344 single-point-of-failure mechanisms does not deploy correctly

revolutionary_discoveries.description: JWST detects unambiguous biosignatures in exoplanet atmospheres
revolutionary_discoveries.explanation: Early observations reveal spectral signatures consistent with biological processes

delayed_launch.description: Further technical issues delay launch to 2024; eventually succeeds
delayed_launch.explanation: Additional testing requirements push timeline back again

space_science_renaissance.description: JWST success triggers massive increase in space science funding globally
space_science_renaissance.explanation: Public enthusiasm translates into political support for exploration programs

2022_russia_ukraine.title: Russia-Ukraine War
2022_russia_ukraine.description: Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine. Largest European land war since WWII. Reshapes European security, energy markets, and global alliances. 300,000+ casualties, nuclear threats, massive displacement.

historical_invasion_stalemate.description: Full invasion; initial Russian failures; prolonged stalemate

no_invasion.explanation: Stronger Western deterrence or Putin calculates costs too high

quick_russian_victory.description: Russia captures Kyiv in weeks; puppet government installed

nato_direct_involvement.description: NATO enters direct combat with Russia

quick_ukrainian_victory.description: Ukrainian counteroffensive succeeds; Russia withdraws by 2023

nuclear_use.description: Russia uses tactical nuclear weapon in Ukraine

frozen_conflict.description: Early ceasefire; frozen conflict along current lines

2022_synthetic_biology.title: Synthetic Biology Regulation
2022_synthetic_biology.description: Advances in DNA synthesis make it possible to create novel organisms and even reconstruct dangerous pathogens from scratch. Biosecurity experts push for mandatory screening of DNA synthesis orders while the synbio industry resists regulation that could slow innovation.

historical_voluntary_screening.description: Voluntary DNA synthesis screening; patchy compliance across industry

mandatory_global_screening.description: International agreement mandates screening of all DNA synthesis orders

unregulated_wild_west.description: Cheap benchtop synthesizers proliferate; regulation impossible to enforce

biosecurity_framework.description: Comprehensive biosecurity framework balances innovation and safety

biohacker_incident.description: Amateur biohacker accidentally releases engineered organism; triggers crackdown

historical_mutiny.description: Prigozhin's march on Moscow; quickly resolved; Prigozhin killed

private_military_norm.description: Private military companies become normalized globally

state_reasserts.description: State reasserts monopoly on military force

2023_ai_acceleration.title: AI Acceleration
2023_ai_acceleration.description: ChatGPT launches late 2022, triggering massive AI investment and rapid capability gains. Generative AI transforms work, education, creative industries. Raises existential risk questions.

historical_rapid.description: Rapid AI advancement; GPT-4, Gemini, Claude in quick succession

slower_progress.description: AI progress plateaus after initial hype; scaling laws hit limits

faster_agi.description: Breakthrough leads to AGI-level systems by 2025
faster_agi.explanation: Unexpected algorithmic breakthrough bypasses scaling needs

open_source_dominant.description: Open source AI models match closed; democratized access

ai_winter.description: AI hype collapses; investment dries up
ai_winter.explanation: Hallucination problems and liability lawsuits halt deployment

china_leads.description: China overtakes US in AI capabilities

historical_expansion.description: BRICS expands to include Saudi Arabia, UAE, others

effective_alternative.description: BRICS becomes effective alternative to Western institutions

paper_tiger.description: BRICS expansion is symbolic; no real impact

2023_gaza_conflict.title: Gaza Conflict Escalation
2023_gaza_conflict.description: Hamas launches surprise attack on Israel on October 7, killing 1,200 people. Israel's military response in Gaza kills tens of thousands and triggers a humanitarian catastrophe. The conflict reshapes Middle East diplomacy, sparks global campus protests, fractures progressive coalitions, and intensifies US domestic polarization.

historical_escalation.description: Prolonged military campaign; humanitarian crisis; global protests; diplomatic isolation

rapid_ceasefire.description: International pressure secures early ceasefire and hostage deal
rapid_ceasefire.explanation: US leverages military aid to compel Israeli restraint; hostage deal succeeds

regional_war.description: Conflict expands to include Hezbollah, Iran; full regional conflagration
regional_war.explanation: Hezbollah opens northern front; Iran directly intervenes; US drawn in

no_october_7.description: Israeli intelligence intercepts Hamas plans; attack is prevented
no_october_7.explanation: Signals intelligence catches the plot; pre-emptive security measures succeed

two_state_catalyst.description: Horror of conflict revives international commitment to two-state solution
two_state_catalyst.explanation: Saudi normalization contingent on Palestinian statehood gains momentum

2023_lahaina.title: Lahaina / Climate Disasters New Normal
2023_lahaina.description: Wildfire destroys the historic town of Lahaina, Maui, killing over 100 people in the deadliest US wildfire in over a century. Demonstrates that climate-driven disasters now threaten affluent, developed-world communities previously considered safe, challenging assumptions about climate vulnerability and preparedness.

historical_devastation.description: Lahaina destroyed; 100+ dead; warning system failures; slow federal response

early_evacuation.description: Warning sirens activated; mass evacuation prevents most fatalities
early_evacuation.explanation: Emergency management systems function as designed; minimal loss of life

climate_policy_shift.description: Lahaina becomes the catalyst for aggressive US climate adaptation investment
climate_policy_shift.explanation: Destruction of an iconic American town shifts political calculus on climate

fire_averted.description: Wind patterns shift; fire contained before reaching Lahaina
fire_averted.explanation: Slightly different weather conditions allow firefighters to establish containment

recurring_disasters.description: Multiple developed-world climate catastrophes in rapid succession normalize loss
recurring_disasters.explanation: Lahaina followed by more fires, floods, and heat waves across the US

historical_mixed.description: Mix of open and closed AI; open source competitive but lagging

open_wins.description: Open source AI matches or exceeds closed models

closed_dominates.description: Closed AI companies dominate; open source marginalized

open_source_incident.description: Open source AI model causes major harm

2023_openai_crisis.title: OpenAI Board Crisis
2023_openai_crisis.description: OpenAI's board fires CEO Sam Altman over concerns about safety and commercialization pace, triggering a five-day crisis. Nearly all employees threaten to quit; Microsoft offers to hire the entire team; Altman is reinstated with a restructured board. The episode crystallizes the tension between AI safety governance and deployment speed.

historical_reinstatement.description: Altman reinstated; safety-focused board members removed; deployment speed prioritized

altman_stays_fired.description: Board's decision holds; OpenAI refocuses on safety-first research
altman_stays_fired.explanation: Enough employees stay; new CEO steers toward cautious development

safety_board_prevails.description: Crisis leads to industry-wide adoption of safety governance structures
safety_board_prevails.explanation: OpenAI crisis becomes a wake-up call; other labs adopt similar oversight

microsoft_absorbs.description: OpenAI collapses; Microsoft absorbs the team and technology
microsoft_absorbs.explanation: Employee exodus to Microsoft creates the world's most powerful AI lab inside Big Tech

no_crisis.description: Board concerns resolved internally without public drama
no_crisis.explanation: Altman and board reach accommodation before any public action

2023_svb_crisis.title: SVB / Banking Wobble
2023_svb_crisis.description: Silicon Valley Bank collapses in the second-largest US bank failure in history, followed by Signature Bank and First Republic. The crisis exposes the hangover from a decade of zero interest rate policy (ZIRP), regional bank fragility, and the speed of social-media-driven bank runs in the digital age.

historical_contained.description: SVB, Signature, First Republic fail; Fed backstops deposits; contagion contained

broader_banking_crisis.description: Contagion spreads to dozens of regional banks; credit crunch follows
broader_banking_crisis.explanation: Social media bank runs overwhelm FDIC capacity; confidence collapses

no_bank_failures.description: SVB manages its bond portfolio adequately; no crisis materializes
no_bank_failures.explanation: Earlier rate normalization or better risk management prevents duration mismatch

systemic_contagion.description: Banking crisis goes global; echoes of 2008 financial crisis
systemic_contagion.explanation: Hidden duration risk across European and Asian banks triggers worldwide panic

regulatory_overhaul.description: Crisis prompts swift, comprehensive banking regulation reform
regulatory_overhaul.explanation: Bipartisan alarm leads to restoration of post-2008 regulatory frameworks

2024_ai_cyber_attacks.title: AI-Powered Cyber Attacks
2024_ai_cyber_attacks.description: Large language models used to generate sophisticated phishing emails, discover software vulnerabilities, and automate exploitation at scale. AI dramatically lowers the barrier to entry for cyber crime and enables personalized social engineering attacks.

historical_escalation.description: AI-powered phishing and exploitation increase cyber damage significantly

ai_defense_advantage.description: AI proves more effective for defense than offense; cyber damage plateaus

autonomous_worms.description: AI-autonomous worms spread and adapt without human guidance

regulated_models.description: AI safety guardrails effectively prevent misuse for cyber attacks

offense_defense_balance.description: AI capabilities balance evenly between attackers and defenders

2024_iss_deorbit.title: ISS Transition
2024_iss_deorbit.description: ISS approaching end of life. Transition to commercial stations (Axiom, Orbital Reef) or gap in human spaceflight capability.

smooth_transition.description: Commercial stations ready; seamless handoff from ISS to Axiom and Orbital Reef
smooth_transition.explanation: Private investment and NASA support ensure continuous human presence in LEO

capability_gap.description: 3-5 year gap with no Western space station; reliance on Tiangong for human research
capability_gap.explanation: Commercial stations delayed; ISS deorbited on schedule leaving capability gap

extended_iss.description: ISS life extended to 2035 as commercial alternatives aren't ready
extended_iss.explanation: Structural concerns managed with repairs; buys time for commercial stations

china_station_dominant.description: Tiangong becomes the only operational station; China leads human spaceflight
china_station_dominant.explanation: No Western replacement materializes in time; international partners join Tiangong

no_replacement.description: No commercial station materializes; human spaceflight enters hiatus
no_replacement.explanation: All commercial station ventures fail financially; gap in human presence in space

2024_mpox.title: Mpox / Disease X Preparedness Test
2024_mpox.description: A new clade of mpox (clade Ib) spreads rapidly in Central Africa and triggers WHO to declare a public health emergency of international concern. Tests whether post-COVID pandemic preparedness systems work and whether global health equity has improved since 2020.

historical_contained.description: WHO declares emergency; vaccines deployed unevenly; outbreak contained but exposes gaps

pandemic_failure.description: Mpox spreads globally; vaccine nationalism repeats COVID failures
pandemic_failure.explanation: Post-COVID fatigue and funding cuts leave health systems unprepared

rapid_global_response.description: Post-COVID systems work as designed; outbreak contained within weeks
rapid_global_response.explanation: Pandemic preparedness investments prove their value; vaccines distributed equitably

ignored_outbreak.description: Outbreak confined to Africa; wealthy nations provide minimal assistance
ignored_outbreak.explanation: Global health equity gains from COVID era prove ephemeral

preparedness_vindicated.description: Mpox tests and validates new global pandemic response architecture
preparedness_vindicated.explanation: Hundred Days Mission and CEPI frameworks deliver rapid countermeasures

2024_pandemic_treaty.title: WHO Pandemic Preparedness Treaty
2024_pandemic_treaty.description: WHO member states negotiate a pandemic preparedness treaty following COVID-19. The agreement aims to ensure equitable access to vaccines, pathogen surveillance sharing, and coordinated response. Sovereignty concerns and geopolitical tensions threaten to derail negotiations.

historical_weak_agreement.description: Watered-down agreement with voluntary commitments; limited enforcement

strong_binding_treaty.description: Binding treaty with enforcement mechanisms; rapid pathogen sharing mandated

treaty_collapses.description: Negotiations fail; nations revert to every-country-for-itself pandemic planning

regional_blocs_only.description: Regional agreements replace global treaty; EU, ASEAN form separate pacts

surveillance_network.description: Global pathogen surveillance network established; early warning system works

2024_tiktok_ban.title: US TikTok Ban Saga
2024_tiktok_ban.description: Congress passes legislation requiring ByteDance to divest TikTok or face a US ban, raising fundamental questions about tech sovereignty, free speech, US-China relations, and government authority over digital platforms. The saga embodies the tension between national security and open internet principles.

historical_ban_saga.description: Ban legislation passes; legal challenges delay enforcement; uncertainty persists

forced_divestiture.description: ByteDance successfully divests TikTok to US-based consortium
forced_divestiture.explanation: Commercial pressures outweigh geopolitical resistance; deal closes

ban_blocked.description: Courts strike down ban as First Amendment violation
ban_blocked.explanation: Supreme Court rules government cannot ban a platform used by 170M Americans

no_legislation.description: Congress fails to pass TikTok legislation; status quo continues
no_legislation.explanation: Lobbying, free speech concerns, and partisan divisions prevent action

reciprocal_tech_war.description: TikTok ban triggers broader US-China tech decoupling and retaliatory bans
reciprocal_tech_war.explanation: China retaliates against Apple and US tech firms; digital iron curtain descends

2024_us_election.title: 2024 US Presidential Election
2024_us_election.description: Trump returns to win the presidency, defeating Vice President Harris. Reflects continued polarization and economic anxiety.

harris_wins.description: Harris wins; first female and Black/South Asian president

third_party.description: Third party candidate disrupts electoral college

2025_ai_regulation.title: AI Regulation
2025_ai_regulation.description: Global response to rapid AI development. EU AI Act, US executive orders, and international frameworks attempt to govern AI development and deployment.

fragmented_national.description: EU regulates heavily; US light-touch; China controls

heavy_regulation.description: Heavy regulation slows AI development globally

2025_brain_computer_interface.title: Brain-Computer Interface Trials
2025_brain_computer_interface.description: Neuralink, Synchron, and others begin human clinical trials for brain-computer interfaces. Initially targeting paralysis and neurological disorders, BCIs could eventually augment healthy human cognition and blur the line between human and machine.

medical_only_slow.description: BCIs help paralysis patients; broader applications remain decades away

rapid_medical_adoption.description: BCIs become standard treatment for paralysis, epilepsy, and depression

safety_setback.description: Serious adverse events in trials; BCI development set back a decade

consumer_bci_2035.description: Non-invasive BCIs reach consumer market by 2035; cognitive enhancement begins

military_first.description: Military invests heavily; soldier augmentation program drives BCI development

2025_climate_tipping.title: Climate Tipping Points
2025_climate_tipping.description: Assessment of whether key climate tipping points have been crossed or avoided. Permafrost, ice sheets, Amazon dieback.

on_track_2_5c.description: World on track for 2.5°C warming by 2100

tipping_point_crossed.description: Major tipping point crossed; accelerating warming

accelerated_action.description: Global mobilization on climate; 1.5°C still possible

technological_breakthrough.description: Breakthrough in cheap carbon capture or fusion

2025_grid_modernization.title: Grid Modernization Crisis
2025_grid_modernization.description: Aging electrical grid infrastructure collides with rapid renewable integration. Intermittent solar and wind require massive transmission upgrades, smart grid technology, and storage. Grid failures and blackouts force urgent modernization decisions.

muddle_through.description: Incremental upgrades barely keep pace; brownouts in peak demand

smart_grid_success.description: Major smart grid investment pays off; seamless renewable integration

grid_failures.description: Cascading grid failures; major blackouts drive political backlash against renewables

distributed_revolution.description: Microgrids and distributed energy bypass centralized grid entirely

regulatory_gridlock.description: Permitting and NIMBY opposition block transmission buildout for years

2025_longevity_research.title: Longevity Research Boom
2025_longevity_research.description: Senolytics, rapamycin analogs, and caloric restriction mimetics enter clinical trials. Billionaire-funded longevity startups promise to extend healthy human lifespan. The question shifts from whether aging can be slowed to who will afford the treatments.

modest_gains.description: Senolytics show modest benefits; healthspan extended by a few years for some

senolytic_breakthrough.description: Senolytic drugs dramatically reduce age-related disease; FDA fast-tracks approval

overhyped_failure.description: Clinical trials fail; longevity bubble bursts and funding collapses

longevity_escape_velocity.description: Combination therapies achieve longevity escape velocity for the wealthy

elite_only_access.description: Effective treatments exist but cost makes them accessible only to the ultra-rich

2025_starship.title: Starship Reaches Orbit
2025_starship.description: SpaceX Starship achieves full orbital flight and landing. If successful, it's the largest and cheapest rocket ever built -- enabling Moon bases, Mars missions, and orbital manufacturing.

on_schedule.description: Starship achieves full orbital success by 2025; largest and cheapest rocket ever
on_schedule.explanation: Iterative development pays off; rapid reusability proven at scale

delayed_2028.description: Technical challenges delay Starship orbital success by three years
delayed_2028.explanation: Heat shield, engine reliability, and regulatory hurdles slow development

partial_success.description: Starship reaches orbit but landing fails; iterative improvement continues
partial_success.explanation: Upper stage performs well but reusable landing proves harder than expected

program_cancelled.explanation: Major accident during flight leads to regulatory shutdown and investor retreat

competitor_beats.description: Blue Origin or Chinese equivalent achieves super-heavy reusability first
competitor_beats.explanation: New Glenn or Long March 9 beat Starship to market; competition reshapes industry

revolutionary_success.description: Starship exceeds expectations; rapid iteration achieves daily launches
revolutionary_success.explanation: Rapid reuse cycle and minimal refurbishment transform space access economics

2026_artemis.title: Artemis Lunar Landing
2026_artemis.description: NASA's return to the Moon. First woman and first person of color on the lunar surface. Whether it leads to sustained presence depends on funding and political will.

successful_landing.description: NASA returns humans to the Moon; first woman and first person of color land on lunar surface
successful_landing.explanation: Starship HLS works as planned; Artemis III achieves historic landing

delayed_2030.description: Artemis lunar landing slips to 2030 due to technical and funding delays
delayed_2030.explanation: HLS development challenges and congressional budget fights push timeline back

cancelled.description: Artemis program cancelled; US lunar ambitions shelved
cancelled.explanation: Political priorities shift; cost overruns and delays erode congressional support

international_mission.description: Artemis becomes joint US/ESA/JAXA mission; international crew lands on Moon
international_mission.explanation: Cost sharing and diplomatic goals transform Artemis into a multinational effort

china_beats_artemis.description: China lands crew on Moon before Artemis; new space race intensifies
china_beats_artemis.explanation: CNSA's steady progress pays off while Artemis faces delays; geopolitical shock

2026_post_quantum_crypto.title: Post-Quantum Cryptography Transition
2026_post_quantum_crypto.description: Global race to migrate encryption systems to post-quantum algorithms before quantum computers can break RSA and ECC. NIST finalizes standards, but migration of legacy systems proves enormously complex. "Harvest now, decrypt later" attacks already underway.

orderly_transition.description: Managed migration to post-quantum standards with minimal disruption

chaotic_scramble.description: Rushed migration causes outages and compatibility failures

quantum_breaks_rsa.description: Quantum computer breaks RSA before transition completes; massive data exposure

crypto_agility.description: Crypto-agile systems enable smooth algorithm swaps as needed

fragmented_standards.description: Competing standards fragment the internet into incompatible crypto zones

2026_taiwan_strait.title: Taiwan Strait Crisis
2026_taiwan_strait.description: Potential military confrontation over Taiwan. China's growing military capability and assertiveness raise the stakes of the most dangerous flashpoint in great power relations.

tension_no_conflict.description: Heightened tensions but no military action

blockade.description: China imposes naval blockade of Taiwan

full_invasion.description: China launches amphibious invasion of Taiwan

us_china_war.description: US-China direct military conflict over Taiwan

peaceful_unification.description: Negotiated unification under 'one country, two systems' framework

2027_alzheimers_treatment.title: Alzheimer's Treatment Breakthrough
2027_alzheimers_treatment.description: After decades of failure, disease-modifying Alzheimer's treatments finally show meaningful clinical benefit. Lecanemab and successors slow cognitive decline, but questions remain about cost, access, and whether prevention is possible.

incremental_progress.description: Anti-amyloid drugs slow decline modestly; not curative but meaningful

true_disease_modification.description: Combination therapies halt Alzheimer's progression; quality of life transformed

prevention_breakthrough.description: Blood biomarker test enables prevention; Alzheimer's incidence drops dramatically

access_crisis.description: Effective treatments cost $100K+/year; only wealthy nations and patients benefit

continued_failure.description: Treatments show minimal real-world benefit; Alzheimer's remains intractable

2027_energy_transition.title: Energy Transition
2027_energy_transition.description: Global energy system transformation. Pace of renewable adoption, nuclear renaissance potential, and fossil fuel phase-out timeline.

nuclear_renaissance.description: SMRs and fusion progress drive nuclear comeback

2028_agi_threshold.title: AGI Threshold
2028_agi_threshold.description: Whether artificial general intelligence is achieved, approaching, or still distant. The most consequential technology question of the century.

no_agi_yet.description: AGI remains distant; narrow AI continues advancing

proto_agi.description: Systems approaching AGI; extremely capable but not general

agi_accident.description: AGI system causes major unintended harm

slow_takeoff.description: Gradual capability increase; AGI emerges incrementally

2028_hydrogen_economy.title: Hydrogen Economy Viability
2028_hydrogen_economy.description: Green hydrogen cost curve reaches critical threshold. Electrolysis powered by cheap renewables could decarbonize heavy industry, shipping, and aviation — sectors resistant to direct electrification. But infrastructure buildout and efficiency losses remain challenges.

niche_role.description: Green hydrogen finds limited use in steel and shipping; not a broad solution

hydrogen_breakthrough.description: Green hydrogen reaches $1/kg; transforms heavy industry and transport

cost_too_high.description: Hydrogen remains 3-5x more expensive than alternatives; adoption stalls

industrial_backbone.description: Hydrogen becomes backbone of industrial decarbonization in EU and Asia

geopolitical_shift.description: Hydrogen-rich nations (Australia, Chile, Morocco) become new energy exporters

contained_quickly.description: New pathogen detected and contained rapidly

moderate_pandemic.description: Moderate pandemic; better prepared than COVID

severe_pandemic.description: Severe pandemic; engineered pathogen or novel virus

2030_japan_population.title: Japan Population Crisis
2030_japan_population.description: Japan's population falls below 120 million for the first time since the 1980s; the village of Nagoro in Tokushima prefecture, famous for its scarecrow residents outnumbering humans, becomes an ironic symbol of the nation's demographic spiral. Prime Minister Ishida convenes an emergency "Future Japan" summit in Osaka.

robot_care_economy.description: SoftBank's 'Kazoku' humanoid caregivers deployed in 14,000 nursing homes across Japan; Toyota's eldercare division surpasses its automotive revenue for the first time
robot_care_economy.explanation: Japan's $80 billion annual investment in care robotics since 2027 pays off; 68% of routine eldercare tasks automated, and South Korea, Germany, and Italy begin licensing the model

immigration_opening.description: Diet passes the landmark 'New Japanese Residency Act,' granting 5-year work visas to 2.4 million Filipino, Vietnamese, and Indonesian workers; Shinjuku's Little Manila district becomes Tokyo's fastest-growing neighborhood
immigration_opening.explanation: After Keidanren warns that 1.8 million jobs will go unfilled by 2032, business lobby overwhelms nativist opposition; PM Ishida frames it as 'enriching Japanese civilization, not diluting it'

managed_decline.description: PM Ishida's 'Graceful Contraction' white paper redefines GDP-per-capita as Japan's primary metric; 340 rural municipalities formally merge into regional cooperatives, closing 2,100 schools but tripling per-student spending in the remainder
managed_decline.explanation: Japan becomes the first major economy to explicitly plan for a smaller population; pension eligibility raised to 70, healthcare rationing introduced through 'quality-adjusted life years' scoring, and the yen strengthens as per-capita wealth rises

crisis_unmanaged.description: Three prime ministers in 18 months as the LDP splinters over pension reform; Hokkaido's last regional hospital closes in December, forcing patients to fly to Sapporo for emergency care
crisis_unmanaged.explanation: Factional warfare inside the LDP paralyzes the Diet; the pension trust fund draws down reserves at 3x projected rates, and Standard & Poor's downgrades Japanese sovereign debt to A- for the first time

pronatalist_success.description: Japan's fertility rate ticks up to 1.58 after the 'Kodomo First' program provides $3,200/month per child and guarantees free childcare from birth; the city of Nagareyama, northeast of Tokyo, sees its under-5 population triple in three years
pronatalist_success.explanation: Total annual spending reaches $140 billion -- more than Japan's defense budget -- with companies required to offer 6 months' paid parental leave for both parents; demographers caution the uptick may be a tempo effect rather than a true reversal

2030_space_tourism.title: Space Tourism Mainstream
2030_space_tourism.description: Blue Origin's 'New Glenn Tourist' vehicle launches its 200th passenger from Cape Canaveral; a Nigerian oil heiress, a retired Osaka schoolteacher, and a 19-year-old TikTok creator share a cabin. The question shifts from 'who can go' to 'should this many rockets be burning this much fuel.'

mainstream_suborbital.description: Virgin Galactic's Mojave terminal processes 40 flights per week; Blue Origin undercuts them at $89,000 a seat; 4,200 people reach space in a single year, more than all government astronauts in history combined
mainstream_suborbital.explanation: Reusable vehicle economics follow the airline playbook -- fill the seats, cut the price; three consecutive years without a fatality builds insurance industry confidence, and Lloyd's of London begins offering standard space tourism policies

orbital_hotels.description: Vast Space opens 'Haven-1' orbital hotel at 400km altitude: 6 suites with floor-to-ceiling Earth-view windows, a zero-gravity bar, and a 14-day stay priced at $28 million; fully booked through 2032 within 72 hours
orbital_hotels.explanation: SpaceX Dragon ferries guests up on biweekly rotations; the station's Instagram account gains 90 million followers in its first month, and three separate reality TV shows compete for filming rights

fatal_accident_setback.description: A Virgin Galactic suborbital vehicle breaks apart during re-entry over New Mexico, killing all six passengers including 31-year-old Indian tech founder Priya Mehta; her final livestream, watched by 12 million people, goes dark at 62km altitude
fatal_accident_setback.explanation: FAA grounds all commercial human spaceflight for 11 months; Congress passes the 'Mehta Safety Act' requiring triple-redundant life support and government-certified pilots; ticket insurers withdraw from the market and three smaller operators fold

niche_luxury.description: Only 73 tourists fly in 2030, each paying $650,000 or more; the passenger manifest reads like the Forbes 400 -- hedge fund managers, tech founders, a Saudi prince -- prompting the Economist to call it 'the world's most expensive selfie opportunity'
niche_luxury.explanation: Vehicle reusability hits diminishing returns on cost reduction; the addressable market for half-million-dollar thrill rides turns out to be narrow, and operators pivot to satellite deployment as their primary revenue while keeping tourism as a prestige sideshow

regulatory_shutdown.description: EU bans leisure spaceflight from European soil over carbon emissions; a Greenpeace blockade of the Boca Chica launch site goes viral; the UN Environmental Programme calculates that 1,000 annual tourist launches would produce more black carbon than all of sub-Saharan Africa
regulatory_shutdown.explanation: The 'Fly Less' climate movement turns its fire on rockets after largely winning the fight against short-haul aviation; even the FAA imposes a 200-launch annual cap for tourist flights, making the economics unworkable for all but SpaceX

2030_us_realignment.title: US Political Realignment
2030_us_realignment.description: The 2030 midterms deliver the most scrambled electoral map since 1932: union plumbers in Youngstown vote alongside Silicon Valley engineers, while suburban Dallas doctors share a ballot line with Montana ranchers. Both parties' internal coalitions are tearing at the seams.

class_based.description: Ohio teamster leader Marco DeSantis and former Amazon warehouse organizer Keisha Washington co-found the 'Working Families Caucus' that sweeps 38 House seats; the GOP loses rural whites without college degrees for the first time since Nixon
class_based.explanation: AI displacement and the gig economy collapse the old culture-war coalitions; a Pew survey finds 71% of Americans now identify their political interests by income bracket rather than party, and both the DNC and RNC lose a third of their donor base

urban_rural_permanent.description: Not a single congressional district within 50 miles of a metro area with 500,000+ people votes Republican; not a single district more than 100 miles from one votes Democrat; the two Americas now have separate de facto policy regimes on guns, abortion, climate, and education
urban_rural_permanent.explanation: Geographic sorting accelerates as remote workers cluster in blue metros and red exurbs harden culturally; the Brookings Institution maps show two archipelagos of governance that share a currency and military but little else

multiparty_emergence.description: The Forward Party wins 4 Senate seats and 22 House seats after ranked-choice voting passes in 14 states; former Republican governor Larry Chen of Arizona and former Democratic congresswoman Aaliyah Brooks of Michigan become its co-chairs
multiparty_emergence.explanation: Alaska and Maine's ranked-choice experiments spread like wildfire after 2028; the 'exhausted middle' finally has a viable vehicle, and Gallup records the first-ever poll where more Americans identify with a third party than with the Democrats

one_party_dominance.description: Democrats hold 58 Senate seats, the House, and 34 governorships after Texas flips blue in 2028; the GOP is locked out of the presidency for three consecutive cycles and RNC chair Vivek Ramaswamy publishes an op-ed titled 'We Are a Regional Party Now'
one_party_dominance.explanation: Latino and Asian-American population growth in Sun Belt suburbs overwhelms Republican margins in rural counties; the Electoral College math becomes nearly impossible for the GOP without winning Pennsylvania AND Georgia AND Arizona simultaneously

continued_polarization.description: The 117th through 121st Congresses pass fewer bills than any stretch since the Civil War; a government shutdown lasting 47 days in 2030 closes national parks during peak summer season, costing gateway communities $2.1 billion
continued_polarization.explanation: Neither party can assemble a governing majority, but neither fractures either; the filibuster survives, gerrymandering entrenches safe seats, and the Supreme Court blocks every structural reform; America governs by executive order and continuing resolution

2031_ai_displacement.title: AI Economic Displacement
2031_ai_displacement.description: McKinsey's annual workforce report lands like a bomb: 28 million white-collar jobs eliminated in OECD countries since 2028, with legal assistants, radiologists, and mid-level software engineers hit hardest. A laid-off insurance adjuster in Columbus, Ohio livestreams his empty office floor -- the video gets 44 million views.

managed_transition.description: The EU's 'Skills Bridge' program retrains 6.2 million workers in AI oversight, elder care, and green construction; Finland's $1,400/month UBI pilot, expanded nationwide in 2029, becomes the template adopted by Canada, Spain, and South Korea
managed_transition.explanation: Germany's IG Metall union negotiates the 'Frankfurt Compact' requiring firms to fund 18-month retraining for every position automated; unemployment peaks at 9.2% in 2030 but falls to 5.8% by late 2032 as the retrained workforce fills new roles in AI auditing and human services

social_crisis.description: US unemployment hits 14.7%; trucker convoys blockade I-95 for three days after autonomous freight eliminates 340,000 long-haul jobs in a single quarter; arson attacks on data centers reported in Lyon, Bangalore, and suburban Atlanta
social_crisis.explanation: The displacement curve is steeper than any model predicted -- call centers, paralegal offices, and accounting firms hollow out simultaneously rather than sequentially; the 'Luddite Summer' of 2031 sees protest movements in 40 countries and three European governments fall

new_jobs_emerge.description: The 'AI whisperer' becomes the fastest-growing job title in America -- 2.1 million people employed as prompt engineers, AI trainers, and human-in-the-loop supervisors; a boom in artisanal 'certified human-made' goods creates a parallel craft economy from Portland to Kyoto
new_jobs_emerge.explanation: Just as ATMs created more bank branches and more tellers, AI tools spawn an ecosystem of human roles managing, correcting, and complementing automated systems; LinkedIn reports that jobs with 'AI' in the title grew 840% between 2028 and 2031

slower_than_expected.description: Despite breathless predictions, only 4.3% of US jobs actually automated by 2031; a Harvard Business School study finds that 60% of enterprise AI deployments stall during integration with legacy systems, and 'AI transformation' budgets quietly become IT maintenance budgets
slower_than_expected.explanation: The gap between demo and deployment turns out to be enormous -- hospitals can't connect AI diagnostics to their 1990s-era records systems, law firms discover AI hallucinations in briefs, and unions in France and Japan negotiate go-slow adoption clauses

bifurcated_economy.description: San Francisco AI engineers earn $900K average comp while former office workers compete for $17/hour 'human touch' service jobs -- elder companionship, artisanal food prep, child tutoring; the Gini coefficient in the US hits 0.49, approaching Brazilian levels
bifurcated_economy.explanation: The economy splits into what economist Daron Acemoglu calls 'the centaur class and the servant class' -- those who work alongside AI multiply their productivity tenfold, while those displaced compete for the shrinking pool of tasks machines cannot or may not do

2031_biotech_regulation.title: Biotechnology Regulation
2031_biotech_regulation.description: A Shenzhen startup quietly cures sickle cell disease in 300 patients using a CRISPR variant that edits bone marrow in vivo -- no extraction needed. The FDA has not approved the therapy; the WHO has no framework for it; and 14,000 Americans are already on flights to Guangdong.

permissive.description: FDA Commissioner Dr. Rachel Okonkwo announces a 'sandbox' approval pathway that cuts gene therapy trials from 8 years to 3; within 18 months, 47 novel CRISPR therapies enter Phase III trials in Boston, Singapore, and Tel Aviv
permissive.explanation: The 'Shenzhen shock' forces Western regulators to choose between losing patients to medical tourism or accelerating approvals; the EU follows with its own fast-track, and by 2033 gene therapies for cystic fibrosis, Huntington's, and type 1 diabetes reach market

strict_global.description: The Geneva Convention on Human Genetic Modification, signed by 128 nations in September 2031, imposes mandatory 5-year monitoring periods and bans germline edits outright; the WHO's new Biotechnology Safety Board gains enforcement teeth with trade-sanction authority
strict_global.explanation: A coalition of European regulators, the Vatican, and a surprising alliance of Chinese scientists who fear domestic corner-cutting push for strict global standards; innovation continues at major research hospitals but the era of garage biotech is firmly closed
